question: When does changing the order between two interventions change an observable outcome?

estimands.note: PREREG Erratum 1: means, not differences. lam_hat, pi_hat are identically 0 under no-carryover / no-period-effect.

mechanism_equation: dz/dt = -(1/tau)[z - u(t)];  u = a_k on intervention k, u = 0 on washout;  y = G z + eps. Closed form: z(t+D) = z(t)e^{-D/tau} + u(1-e^{-D/tau})

parameter_table.name: t_p
parameter_table.source_or_assumption: DERIVED: R1 trial duration 'twice weekly for 90 min over 3 months' -> 90 d

parameter_table.name: t_w
parameter_table.source_or_assumption: SOURCE: R1 Table 4 (Sparrow et al.), washout period = 0 d

parameter_table.name: t_o
parameter_table.source_or_assumption: ASSUMPTION: read-out at the end of period 2, t_o = t_p. Swept: it is a design lever

parameter_table.name: tau
parameter_table.source_or_assumption: OVERIFIERAD (no primary value retrieved). FREE PARAMETER; default t_p/10, swept over 4 decades

parameter_table.name: a_A
parameter_table.source_or_assumption: IDENTIFIED: period1_raw/S with period1_raw = 4.8 pt (R1 Table 2A, 25.0 - 20.2)

parameter_table.name: a_B
parameter_table.source_or_assumption: ASSUMPTION: comparator (usual care) writes no latent state

parameter_table.name: G
parameter_table.source_or_assumption: CONVENTION: latent state expressed in outcome units; only G*a_A is identified

parameter_table.name: sigma_w
parameter_table.source_or_assumption: DERIVED: R1 Table 2A SEs*sqrt(n) -> 3.19 (P1) and 3.69 (P2) pt

parameter_table.name: n_seq
parameter_table.source_or_assumption: SOURCE: R1 Table 2A, N=7 (Exercise->UC) and N=9 (UC->Exercise)

table.justification: [pt] + [pt] x dimensionless = [pt]  (u is an attractor LEVEL, not a rate)
attractor level in [pt], independent of tau [d]

unit_check.scale_check: all estimands in [pt]; all times in [d]; G, alpha dimensionless

published_reference.table: Table 2A (means/SEs) and Table 4 (washout = 0 d), Front Neurol 2023;14:1197281

calibration.identified_from: period1_raw_contrast = 4.8 pt (the only significance-supported quantity in R1)
calibration.not_calibrated_to: lam_hat = 1.5 pt, which is below its own MDC of 2.45 pt -- calibrating to it would fit noise

analytic_max_over_tau_published_design.assumption: t_w = 0 and t_o = t_p; K = G(a_A - a_B)/2

detection_design_levers.analytic_rule: lam_hat is a difference of two order-1 terms, so it is bounded by a_A/8 at t_w=0, t_o=t_p; the only lever that can exceed the MDC is t_o -> 0 (read the outcome immediately at the switch) or t_p -> inf with t_o << tau.

tau.swing_note: base contrast is < 1% of the MDC; a relative swing is not interpretable -- use order_detectable_at_t_w_0 and t_w_star_days

a_A.swing_note: base contrast is < 1% of the MDC; a relative swing is not interpretable -- use order_detectable_at_t_w_0 and t_w_star_days

sigma_w.swing_note: base contrast is < 1% of the MDC; a relative swing is not interpretable -- use order_detectable_at_t_w_0 and t_w_star_days

G.swing_note: base contrast is < 1% of the MDC; a relative swing is not interpretable -- use order_detectable_at_t_w_0 and t_w_star_days

t_p.swing_note: base contrast is < 1% of the MDC; a relative swing is not interpretable -- use order_detectable_at_t_w_0 and t_w_star_days

t_o.swing_note: base contrast is < 1% of the MDC; a relative swing is not interpretable -- use order_detectable_at_t_w_0 and t_w_star_days

FC1.note: identification, i.e. exact by construction -- it is NOT an independent test; the independent test is FC2

FC2.verdict: model predicts an order effect smaller than the resolution of the published data

FC4.assumption: t_w = 0 and t_o = t_p; K = G(a_A - a_B)/2
